```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# This notebook is designed to render even when the erbot package cannot be
# loaded (for example on a machine without the package installed): the
# narrative and tables always render; only the live demo chunk needs erbot.
find_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
  d <- normalizePath(start, winslash = "/", mustWork = FALSE)
  for (i in 1:6) {
    if (file.exists(file.path(d, "DESCRIPTION"))) return(d)
    parent <- dirname(d)
    if (parent == d) break
    d <- parent
  }
  NA_character_
}
repo_root <- find_root()
can_run <- FALSE
load_msg <- "erbot could not be loaded; the demo chunk will be skipped."
if (!is.na(repo_root)) {
  old_wd <- getwd()
  setwd(repo_root)
  can_run <- tryCatch({
    if (requireNamespace("pkgload", quietly = TRUE)) {
      pkgload::load_all(".", quiet = TRUE)
    } else {
      library(erbot)
    }
    TRUE
  }, error = function(e) {
    load_msg <<- paste0("erbot could not be loaded: ", conditionMessage(e))
    FALSE
  })
  setwd(old_wd)
}
```

## Purpose

On 25 September the advisor gave five requests. This notebook is the response,
organised the same way, and it is deliberately explicit about the difference
between **done**, **implemented but not yet run**, and **not done**.

Nothing in this notebook claims a run that has not happened. The live demo at
the end is off by default (`run_demo: false`); set it to `true` in VS Code and
re-render to run a scenario in the meeting.

## 1. Clean code: scenarios you can ask for by name

The pipeline already had one entry point (`er_run()`), but no named scenarios
and no explained errors. Four presets now exist:

```{r presets}
if (can_run) {
  er_scenario_presets()
} else {
  data.frame(
    scenario = c("smoke", "screening", "full", "unsupervised_quick"),
    purpose = c(
      "Verify the pipeline runs end-to-end.",
      "Broad first pass over clustering methods.",
      "Reportable run, consensus merging.",
      "Fast unsupervised pass, no ground truth."
    )
  )
}
```

One command runs a scenario from the repository root:

```bash
Rscript scripts/run_scenario.R --scenario smoke --data cora
```

When a run fails, the error is rewritten into three parts — **stage**,
**reason**, **next step** — covering the failures we actually hit: missing
files, missing packages, a label column leaking into features, pair-budget
explosions, an all-NA model sweep, and infeasible split quotas.

**Honest gap.** The Scenario 1 / Scenario 3 harness behind the v3 report is
not in this repository (the repo contains Protocol A/B instead). That code is
in the local VS Code workspace and still has to be merged; tonight's work
cleans the erbotv2 interface around it.

## 2. Why things succeed or fail: mechanism cards

Eight cards (full text in `docs/mechanism-cards-2026-10-01.md`). The three to
be able to say without notes:

- **QDA** was refused because the two-way interaction expansion made the
  design matrix wider than the positive class (FEBRL1: 9 features → 45
  predictors vs 37–47 positive pairs). With interactions off, QDA fits in
  **20/20** cells. Admissibility was a design property, not a dataset property.
- **Logistic regression** fails differently: fitted probabilities of exactly
  0/1 mean complete separation. No design change repairs that; a penalised fit
  (Firth) is the right path, and it has not yet been wired in.
- **CORA seed 6666** had the best validation ARI (0.946) and the worst test ARI
  (0.415), with recall 0.996 but precision 0.291 — 155 missed pairs against
  102,684 false co-clustered pairs and a 496-record predicted entity (truth:
  199). It failed by over-merging through transitive chains, which ARI alone
  does not reveal.

The other cards cover validation ties (the recorded "winner" is a tie-breaking
artifact over an equivalence set of up to 60 models), sparse positives
(Restaurant test partitions hold 9–13 positive pairs), Affiliation's two-sided
failure on a single weak feature, the candidate universe as part of the task
definition, and what Scenario 1 vs Scenario 3 each can and cannot claim.

## 3. Positive ratio: a design decision, proposed not smuggled

The previous discipline — split records without looking at gold, never redraw
a seed — exists to prevent seed-hacking. The proposed design keeps that spirit
and makes the label use explicit and pre-registered:

- Split **entities** (never records or pairs) into Fit / Validation / Test,
  balancing record fractions and positive-pair quotas under one fixed seed.
  Infeasible quotas error out with the achieved counts; nothing is redrawn.
- Augment positives **only inside Fit** (resampled to a target Fit
  prevalence), labelled simulated prevalence, reported separately forever.
- Validation and Test always keep natural prevalence.

Implemented in `R/22-positive_ratio.R` (`er_stratified_three_way_split()`,
`er_augment_fit_pairs()`, `er_positive_ratio_report()`). **Decision needed:**
is the label-aware pre-registered split acceptable, and should the canonical
rule be quotas or a Fit prevalence target?

## 4. New datasets

**D10K.** The current loader keeps only `Id` + `Aggregate Value`, which gives
one text field, not a similarity matrix. `R/23-d10k_similarity.R` adds the
parsing layer (structure-aware: key=value or consistent separators, otherwise
a single text field) and returns the combined sparse similarity matrix `S`
through the existing NA-aware combiner. Not yet run on the real
`10Kfull.csv`, which is not in this worktree.

**MusicBrainz 20K.** Leipzig source checked: 19,375 records, 10,000 clusters,
16,250 duplicate pairs, five sources, high-corruption DAPO duplicates.
`er_build_musicbrainz()` splits the raw file into a model table (title,
artist, album, year, length, language, number, source) and a gold table —
`CID` goes to gold only and can never become a feature. `er_load()` and
`er_load_gold()` know the dataset; the catalog is updated. The raw header is
verified (comma-delimited:
`TID,CID,CTID,SourceID,id,number,title,length,artist,album,year,language`),
though the values are messy — length can be `1m 58sec`, year can be `75` or
`null` — so type handling is left to `er_diagnose()`. The builder itself has
not yet run in an R environment.

## 5. Paper direction

Brief: `docs/paper-direction-brief-2026-10-01.md`.

**Recommendation: scaling / blocking as the primary direction.** It continues
the candidate-space work (mechanism card 7), needs the least new machinery,
and sits where supervision is strongest. Its ownable question is the one the
advisor raised: record-level blocking and pair-level blocking are different
objects, and a method contribution has to respect that distinction rather
than produce another benchmark table.

Deep learning stays warm with one cheap probe: an embedding view on
Affiliation — the dataset whose single weak feature fails in both directions —
under the existing protocol. A large, explainable gain there would justify a
second paper or a pivot.

re-render to run the pipeline here, in the meeting.

```{r demo}
if (isTRUE(params$run_demo) && can_run) {
  res <- er_run_scenario(params$scenario, data = params$dataset, verbose = TRUE)
  cat(sprintf("Scenario '%s' on '%s': %d records, %d clusters.\n",
              params$scenario, params$dataset,
              nrow(res$predictions), length(unique(res$clusters))))
  if (!is.null(res$performance)) print(res$performance)
} else if (isTRUE(params$run_demo)) {
  cat(load_msg, "\n")
} else {
  cat("Demo skipped (run_demo = false). Set run_demo: true and re-render to run it.\n")
}
```

## Decisions to ask for today

1. Positive-ratio design (Item 3): label-aware pre-registered split — acceptable?
   Quotas or Fit prevalence target as the canonical rule?
2. Paper direction (Item 5): scaling/blocking as primary, deep learning as the
   Affiliation probe — or the other way around?
3. D10K (Item 4a): confirm the canonical raw file (`10Kfull.csv`) so the
   similarity layer can be run and checked against its real format.
